metaTitle: Philippines to Korea Visa: Do You Need One? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Yes — Filipino passport holders need a visa for South Korea (C-3 tourist), but the visa fee is FREE. Where to apply, the documents and where to get each, and processing time — step by step.

verdict.headline: Yes — Filipino passport holders need a visa, but it's FREE.
verdict.sub: You apply for the C-3 tourist visa before travelling to mainland Korea. The upside: there's no visa fee, processing is quick, and since Feb 2026 you no longer submit 3-month bank statements.
verdict.entry: Single entry (multiple-entry possible for qualified travelers)

highlights.title: No visa fee
highlights.body: The C-3 tourist visa is free of charge for Philippine passport holders. Watch out for agencies that add their own service charges.

highlights.title: Simplified since 20 Feb 2026
highlights.body: Applicants in the Philippines are no longer required to submit the last 3 months' bank statements. Employees show ITR + Certificate of Employment instead.

highlights.title: Jeju Island — separate visa-free entry
highlights.body: There are limited visa-free entry options (starting with Jeju Island). These are separate from the mainland tourist visa.

tldr: The C-3 tourist visa is required for mainland Korea — but it's FREE.
Fill the form at visa.go.kr, then submit via the Korean Embassy or an accredited travel agency.
Employees: bring ITR + Certificate of Employment. Business owners: DTI/SEC + business permit.
Since Feb 2026 you no longer need 3-month bank statements. Processing is about 3–5 business days.

items.title: Confirm the visa type
items.detail: For tourism, apply for the C-3 short-term tourist visa.

items.title: Fill the form at visa.go.kr
items.detail: Complete the application form on the Korea Visa Portal — the only official site — then print and sign it.

items.title: Prepare your documents
items.detail: Gather the checklist below. Employees center on ITR + Certificate of Employment; business owners on registration + permit.

items.title: Submit to the Embassy / accredited agency
items.detail: Lodge your application with the Embassy of Korea in the Philippines or an embassy-accredited travel agency.

items.title: No visa fee to pay
items.detail: The visa itself is free. If you use a travel agency, they may charge their own handling fee — the embassy fee is zero.

items.title: Wait ~3–5 business days
items.detail: Processing is quick, but allow more time around Korean holidays (Chuseok, Seollal).

items.title: Collect your passport
items.detail: Pick up your passport and check the visa details right away.

documents.title: Document checklist — with where & how to get each
documents.intro: For each item, here is where to obtain it and what it must show. Requirements differ for employees, business owners and students.

rows.how: Complete on the Korea Visa Portal, print, sign.
A bank certificate of your account. Note: since 20 Feb 2026, 3-month bank statements are no longer required.
Income Tax Return proving your employment income.
On company letterhead: position, salary, and approved leave dates.
DTI (sole proprietor) or SEC (corporation) registration, plus your business/mayor's permit.
Reservations/itinerary are enough — don't pay for a ticket before approval.

funds.title: "How do I prove I can afford the trip?"
funds.body: Since Feb 2026, you no longer submit 3-month bank statements — a bank certificate plus your ITR/employment (or business) proof carries the financial story. The aim is to show stable income and strong ties to the Philippines.
tips: Employees: ITR + Certificate of Employment are the core of your file.
Business owners: registration + business permit + a bank certificate.
Being sponsored? Add the sponsor's documents and proof of relationship.

items.d: The embassy visa is FREE. Only agency handling fees are legitimate extras.
Missing ITR or COE. These are now the heart of a Filipino applicant's file.
Buying non-refundable tickets before approval — a reservation is enough.
Jeju visa-free options don't cover mainland Korea travel.
Processing slows around Chuseok/Seollal — apply earlier.

items.q: Do Filipinos need a visa for Korea?
items.a: Yes for mainland Korea — you apply for a C-3 tourist visa before travelling. It is free of charge. Jeju Island has separate visa-free entry.

items.q: How much is the visa fee?
items.a: There is no visa fee for the C-3 tourist visa for Philippine passport holders. A travel agency may charge its own service fee, but the embassy fee is zero.
Since 20 Feb 2026, 3-month bank statements are no longer required. Employees show ITR + Certificate of Employment; business owners show registration + permit.
About 3–5 business days, longer around Korean holidays like Chuseok and Seollal.
At the Embassy of Korea in the Philippines or through an embassy-accredited travel agency.

items.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
items.a: Multiple-entry visas are possible for qualified travelers (e.g., strong travel history). Ask the embassy about current eligibility.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
items.a: Entry-document rules such as the e-Arrival Card can still apply on arrival. Check the current rules near your travel date.
